response: The prognosis of patients with allergic contact dermatitis from an occupational cohort is indeed dependent on the omnipresence of the allergen. If the allergen is ubiquitous and cannot be avoided, the prognosis is generally poorer, with higher rates of persistent or recurrent dermatitis. In contrast, if the allergen is identifiable and can be avoided or minimized, the prognosis is better, with higher rates of improvement or complete recovery.
